summary: The current mapped candidate preserves all 21 criteria and the accepted architecture under the authorized log-access/header change. Its explicit owned-record mode is coherent as a future versioned helper extension. No mandatory compatibility correction is required; native proof and G1 implementation remain outstanding.

compatibility_findings.finding: The current runtime-adapter edition replaces the stale live binding while retaining the original Phase 001 edition as historical evidence. The earlier keep-live-document-unchanged statement is explicitly corrected and cannot restore obsolete bytes.

Summary/query delivery and a bounded first-record header establish scoped access/identity only. The 131072-byte newline-terminated header does not certify later log bytes. Full native history/page/prefix/equality, complete role/problem input, wire/cell and authenticated callback checks remain independent. Reader-incarnation and stat-bound cursor checks must remain current after same-ID resume.

The explicitly selected owned-record mode requires authenticated allocation, real IDs/lineage, canonical log path/device/inode/header, bounded consistent owned-row reads, schema/identity checks, fixed canaries, current caller/grant/owner provenance, startup-writer closure and final owned-process observations. Returned filenames alone do not establish ownership.

Unrelated index contents are correctly labeled unobserved. This avoids both an unsupported unchanged claim and an automatic ambient allowance. Existing strict modes, authority limits and filesystem/tool/network/publication denials retain their semantics.

The current owning helper accepts storage schema 1 and assumes a whole preservation inventory, including history_file_metadata in bind_storage and unchanged_unlisted_metadata results. The candidate correctly requires explicit owner version dispatch and focused tests before G1 materialization, rather than a runner-only bypass.

Three permanent actors plus a fourth loaded incarnation of the same generic worker preserve generic identity rules. G1 retains actual reservation/read/activation/writer-transfer, implementation/independent behavior verification, same-ID resume, new role/input acknowledgment, helper reset, control/old-epoch denial, separate memory/ontology grants and final owner/Task stop reconciliation. The 18-start/120-cell target requires measured preparation and exact bounds; it is not a provider-call cap or native pass. The separate 61-start P1 prerequisite may retire while its partial result remains historical. Remaining NP001-014 outcomes must be mapped to G2-G4 and final source revalidation.
